# Extract Audio from Video

- Route: `/tools/extract-audio-from-video`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `extract-audio-from-video`

## Summary

Save the audio track from any video as a clean MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, or OGG file. (Video tools)

## Details

Every video container carries its audio as a separate stream, so getting the sound out does not involve the picture at all. This page asks FFmpeg to select the first audio stream, ignore the video, and encode that stream into the format you pick: MP3 for anything that plays music, WAV or FLAC when you want the samples untouched, M4A or AAC for a small file that phones handle natively, or OGG Vorbis. Before it starts, the server checks with ffprobe that an audio stream exists, because FFmpeg would otherwise write an empty file without complaint.
### What it does
- Selects the first audio stream (-map 0:a:0) from MP4, MOV, M4V, WebM, MKV, AVI and the other common video containers and discards the video (-vn).
- Encodes MP3 with libmp3lame at quality 2 (variable bitrate averaging about 190 kbps), WAV as 16-bit PCM, M4A or AAC at 192 kbps, FLAC losslessly, or OGG with libvorbis at quality 5.
- Keeps the original sample rate and channel count; nothing is resampled or mixed down.
- Refuses a video with no audio stream up front with the message that there is nothing to extract.
- Returns a single audio file named after the original with the chosen extension.
### How to use it
1. Upload the video: Any common container; the file goes straight to our storage bucket and the API picks it up.
2. Choose the audio format: MP3 is preset. WAV and FLAC are lossless; M4A and AAC are compact; OGG is the open lossy option.
3. ffprobe confirms an audio stream exists: A silent video stops here with a clear error instead of producing an empty file.
4. FFmpeg encodes the stream: One command with -map 0:a:0 -vn and the encoder for your format.
5. Download the audio: The file lives in the job folder until its retention window ends.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, webm, mkv, avi, m4v
- Output: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, flac, ogg
- We extract the first audio stream. Videos without any audio stream return a clear error instead of an empty file.
### Technical details
- The command is ffmpeg -y -i input -map 0:a:0 -vn <encoder args> output (runExtractAudio in specialized_tools.go). -vn means the video stream is never decoded, which is why extraction is fast even on 4K sources.
- MP3 uses -c:a libmp3lame -q:a 2, the LAME V2 variable-bitrate setting, which averages around 190 kbps on music and less on speech. WAV uses -c:a pcm_s16le, so a 44.1 kHz stereo source costs about 10.1 MB per minute and a 48 kHz source about 11 MB per minute.
- M4A and AAC both use the native FFmpeg AAC encoder with -b:a 192k. FLAC is lossless and typically lands at 50 to 70 percent of the WAV size. OGG uses -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5, roughly 160 kbps.
- No -ar or -ac flag is passed, so the output keeps the source sample rate and channel layout; 5.1 surround stays 5.1 in WAV and FLAC, while MP3 will carry at most two channels.
- Only stream 0:a:0 is mapped. A file with a commentary track or a second language keeps whichever track is listed first in the container.
- Extraction is a specialized mode: the upload is not queued for the automated content analysis that standard conversions receive, and the quality, resize and effect controls of the video converter do not apply.
### When not to use it
Do not use this page to improve the sound; it copies what is there, and a noisy or distant recording stays noisy. The Clean Voice and Remove Background Noise tools are built for that. Do not expect a WAV to recover quality that the video lost; the source track is almost always lossy AAC, so a WAV is a faithful copy of a compressed signal, not a studio master. If the video has two language tracks and you need the second one, this tool only takes the first. And if what you really want is the words, the transcriber reads the audio and gives you text and captions directly.
### Use cases
- Audio-only episodes: Publish the sound of a recorded video interview as a podcast MP3.
- Transcription prep: Feed an 18 minute recording to a transcriber as a 25 MB MP3 instead of a 540 MB MP4.
- Sound design and sampling: Pull a WAV from a clip to reuse ambience or music in another edit.
- Lecture notes: Keep the audio of a class recording for listening on the go.
### FAQ
Q: Which audio formats can I extract to, and which are lossless?
A: MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC and OGG. WAV and FLAC are lossless copies of the decoded track. MP3 (about 190 kbps VBR), M4A and AAC (192 kbps) and OGG (quality 5) are lossy but above the bitrate of most video sound tracks.
Q: How big will the extracted audio be?
A: WAV is about 10.1 MB per minute at 44.1 kHz stereo, or 11 MB at 48 kHz. MP3 at this page setting is about 1.4 MB per minute, M4A and AAC about 1.4 MB per minute at 192 kbps, OGG about 1.2 MB per minute. FLAC usually lands between half and two thirds of the WAV size.
Q: Does extraction change the sample rate or stereo image?
A: No. FFmpeg is run without -ar or -ac, so the output keeps the source sample rate and channel layout. A 48 kHz stereo track stays 48 kHz stereo.
Q: What happens if my video has no audio?
A: The server probes the file first and stops with the message that there is nothing to extract. The operation is refunded, and no empty file is produced.
Q: My video has two audio tracks; which one do I get?
A: The first one in the container, stream 0:a:0. There is no track picker yet. If the one you need is second, remux or re-export the video with that track first.
Q: Is extracting audio free, and how long a video can I upload?
A: Yes. Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. Current limits are listed on the pricing page.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Send visitors here when they want the sound from a video saved as its own file: "get the mp3 from this video", "rip the audio track out of my video", "pull the sound out of a clip", "save the audio of my recording". The video itself is left alone: this makes a new audio file. Outputs MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC or OGG from the first audio track.
When to send them elsewhere: It copies the sound as is; to improve it use Clean Voice Audio (clean-voice-audio) or Remove Background Noise (remove-background-noise). For the spoken words as text use Transcribe Video (transcribe-video), and for a silent video use Extract Video Without Audio (extract-video-only-from-video).
Related tools: transcribe-video (get the words instead); clean-voice-audio (improve the voice); remove-background-noise (reduce noise); remove-vocals-from-song (strip vocals from music); video-trimmer (cut the video first)
